newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ's forex/inflation coefficient left unchanged.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ's forex/inflation coefficient left unchanged.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Don Brash said on Friday the bank had left intact its coefficient for assessing the impact of currency changes on inflation.
The bank assumes every one percent rise in the currency's Trade-Weighted Index translates to a 0.3 percent decrease in consumer prices.
"We think on balance that 0.3 (percent) is still the appropriate coefficient," Brash said.
He said it appeared to be taking longer for the disinflation effects of an appreciating currency to feed through into prices in a situation where demand was quite strong.
"But at this point, we don't have a good reason for a different number," Brash added. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
